name: Next-command forecast errors split by the following pulse
reason: The 10-min next-command window of the two mixed Test C conditions (0.25 and 25 ng/ml) holds ten forecast origins per cell, before two different pulses. The B3 increment raised the condition-equal 10-min error of this window by 7.2% (0.03306 to 0.03544; -4.6% at 0.25 and +23.4% at 25 ng/ml); the natural probe at 114 min suggests that B3 overestimates recovery after the long command, and the first 3/20 probe that it underestimates recovery 20 min after a short pulse. The saved scores do not separate the two groups of origins.
models: the frozen 10-min nested models of results/nested/nested_results.json (main/10: C, O, M, H with the selected sigma), persistence P, and the same forecast rows as nested_phase_detail.py; no fitting and no selection
definition: next-command rows are origins t with a pulse starting in (t, t + 10]; mixed pulses are [1,4), [24,54) and [114,119) min (calibrate_fgf2.segments); group 'before_30min_pulse' = origins 14, 16, 18, 20, 22 min (10-18 min after the initial 3-min pulse, onset 24 min); group 'before_5min_probe' = origins 104, 106, 108, 110, 112 min (50-58 min after the 30-min pulse, onset 114 min); the pulse at 1 min has no rows because origins before 10 min are excluded by the warmup
outputs: per condition and group: rows, cells, origins, 10-min RMSE of P, C, O, M and H; mean signed error (forecast minus target) of each model; mean B3 increment b3_delta and mean realized 10-min change (target minus current reporter); MSE difference M - O; number of cells whose mean squared error over the group's five origins is larger for M than for O; per group the condition-equal pooled RMSE (square root of the mean of the per-condition MSEs) and relative change RMSE_M / RMSE_O - 1 (positive: the increment raises the error); per condition and pooled, each group's share of the window's M - O MSE increase = (MSE_M - MSE_O)_group / (2 (MSE_M - MSE_O)_window) (each cell contributes five rows to each group); 95% percentile intervals from 2000 resamples of cells within each condition (seed 20261011) for the per-group M - O MSE difference and the signed errors of O and M
reading: The increase is located before the probe that follows the long command if, at 25 ng/ml, that group's share is >= 0.75 and its M - O MSE difference has a 95% interval above 0; it is consistent with B3 overestimating recovery if, at 25 ng/ml in that group, M's mean signed error is positive and exceeds O's; a negative M signed error before the 30-min pulse would be consistent with the 3/20 probe (B3 underestimating recovery after a short pulse); otherwise the paper states that the split does not locate the error. In every case these are the probe cells, so the result is not independent confirmation.
check: origins of each group exactly as defined in both conditions; rows per group = 5 x cells (435/435 and 420/420); every next-command row in exactly one group (the run stops on any other onset); the SHA-256 of nested_results.json as pinned; combining the two groups (row-weighted MSE) reproduces the per-condition next-command RMSE of phase_detail.json within 1e-12; on failure no result is interpreted and a corrected version is frozen before the single rerun
reporting: All results reported whatever their direction; descriptive breakdown of frozen models on inspected roles; five origins per group and condition. The groups also differ in the following pulse (30-min versus 5-min), the time since the previous pulse (10-18 versus 50-58 min) and the length of reporter history, so a difference between groups localizes the error but is not attributable to the previous command alone.
